I am 65 years old and have farmed these fields in Quzhou County for over 40 years. I only finished primary school, but I know this land well. Every year I stick to what works: winter wheat followed by summer maize. That is what my neighbors do, and that is what the grain merchant expects. I have eight mu in total—enough for wheat and maize on the same plot, rotated season by season.

Right now it is early spring, and my wheat is already in the ground from last October. I will give it one more flood irrigation when the weather warms, plus a top-dressing of urea at green-up. I usually irrigate four times in total for wheat: winter water, green-up, jointing, and filling. I rotary-till before sowing wheat every autumn, and I sow about 30 jin of improved seed per mu. For fertilizer I spread 100 jin of compound and top-dress with nitrogen once. I spray insecticide twice, herbicide once, and fungicide once because the mildew gets bad when it is humid. I expect about 1,000 jin of wheat per mu if the weather holds.

After harvest in early June, I will plant maize the same day—I do not till again, just sow directly into the stubble. I use hybrid seed, Nongda 372 or something similar, about one package per mu. I put down compound fertilizer at sowing and irrigate twice, at jointing and filling. Maize needs less care than wheat, but I spray for armyworm and weeds, about three times total. If all goes well I will get around 1,100 jin per mu. I have tried cotton and other crops before, but at my age I do not want surprises. Wheat and maize give me steady grain to sell and straw to feed my animals. That is my plan.
